context: The existing test (test-data/claim-tests/thompson-growth-form/thompson1917-ch07-04/result.json) scored the human corneal endothelium as its most regular tissue (75% of junctions within 15 degrees of 120, 0 T-junctions) from one Wikimedia image, and found in Drosophila wing that junction angles approach 120 degrees only as cell division stops. Clinical ophthalmology measures the same geometry routinely: specular microscopy reports percent hexagonal cells (HEX), cell-area coefficient of variation (CV) and endothelial cell density (ECD), and reads falling HEX as corneal stress or cell loss (aging, surgery, Fuchs' dystrophy). This scouting locates datasets that would let a follow-up test ask whether departure from hexagonal packing tracks cell loss and donor age in a non-dividing human epithelium, i.e. the reverse reading of the ch07-04 finding. Recorded as idea-corneal-hex-clinical in decisions/ideas.json (reach-synthesis).

datasets.name: Measurements of ex vivo human corneal endothelium using Voronoi segmentation (Brookes, University of Auckland / New Zealand National Eye Bank, 2017)

checked.method: GET https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/5701087 (title, description with field list, files, licence); file not downloaded

variables_present: per-cell polygon side count or per-image hexagonal fraction in human corneal endothelium
endothelial cell density (cells/mm^2) per image or eye
cell-area coefficient of variation per image or eye
variables_missing: a covariate that indexes cell loss or settling: donor age, time since surgery, disease status, or storage duration
datasets.scope: 354,998 cells from 2,000 routine assessment images of 678 organ-cultured donor corneas from 351 donors, measured by Voronoi segmentation before release for transplantation. One CSV, Human_Corneal_Endothelium.csv (105 MB).
datasets.evidence: Figshare API description lists 40 columns including per image: Mean Cell Area, Cell Area CV, Mean Cell Density, 4- to 9-sides cell counts and % area, Mean Hexagonal Cell Regularity, Number of Pleomorphs, Mean Cell Sides, Cell Sides CV, Shape Index; per cell: Cell Area, Number of Sides, Hexagonal Cell Regularity, Shape Index. Donor age is not in the listed columns. Method paper: Brookes NH, Cell Tissue Bank 2017;18:167-183, doi 10.1007/s10561-017-9622-9 (cited in the record description, not fetched).
datasets.note: Side counts, not junction angles: hexagonal fraction and sides CV are the Lewis-law / topological face of the 120-degree claim (compare thompson1917-ch07-09), not a direct angle measurement. Voronoi segmentation imposes straight walls and three-way vertices by construction, so this data cannot test the 'by threes' half of the claim. Large enough to replace the single Wikimedia image for the 'settled human epithelium is near-hexagonal' reading.

summary: No public dataset carries junction angles for human corneal endothelium. Two University of Auckland datasets (CC BY 4.0) carry per-cell side counts and hexagonal regularity from Voronoi segmentation: 354,998 cells from 678 donor corneas (10.17608/k6.auckland.5701087, no donor age in the listed columns) and a small paired pre/post-transplant table with donor age, storage time and topological charge (10.17608/k6.auckland.31360192). A Dryad CC0 table gives instrument-reported HEX/CV/ECD for 111 healthy children (10.5061/dryad.hhmgqnkjc). Together they support a side-count (Lewis-law) reading of the 120-degree claim in a settled human epithelium, and a test of whether hexagonality falls with cell loss, but not a direct angle measurement, and Voronoi segmentation assumes three-way vertices so it cannot test the 'by threes' half. Clinical PDFs on Zenodo report ECD/HEX/CV only as cohort summaries.
